statement: Under the literal independent-row convention G_alpha=<c_1>x...x<c_k> on disjoint row blocks, every product K_alpha x K_beta for partitions alpha,beta of n has a nonnegative integral K-species coproduct decomposition for n=1,2,3, but K_(2,2) x K_(4) has no such decomposition in degree four. Its unique degree-four cycle-index expansion is 2 K_(2,2) - 2 K_(2,1,1) + 2 K_(1,1,1,1). Therefore degree four is the first failure of nonnegative independent-row K-basis closure, in exactly the sense specified in problem.md; no claim is made about closed formulas in a larger molecular-species basis or the rest of Open Problem 5.1.
contribution: A complete exact resolution of the frozen problem: a hand proof identifies the two S_4 double cosets and the negative unique basis coefficient, proves genuine species closure for every pair below degree four, and is corroborated by an exhaustive rational certificate plus a separately implemented replay. The value is the convention-specific smallest-degree obstruction; no priority claim is asserted.
